title: Native DRAM Cache: Re-architecting DRAM as a Large-Scale Cache for Data Centers
problem: Data center CPUs with increasing core counts require larger Last-Level Caches, but using DRAM as a cache presents significant challenges in latency and energy efficiency.
motivation: Scaling core counts in modern data centers demands higher-capacity caching strategies that can serve as effective Last-Level Cache without excessive latency and power penalties.
method: Native DRAM Cache (NDC) moves the cache lookup work — checking if requested data is in the cache and selecting where to find it — directly into DRAM hardware instead of separate circuits. It accomplishes this by repurposing transistors that DRAM already has for routine maintenance (precharge transistors) to run these lookups. This technique, called Caching-In-Memory, allows DRAM to work as a large, flexible cache with lower latency and energy consumption than traditional designs.
key_novelty: The core idea is to perform cache lookups (tag matching and way selection) directly within DRAM by reusing precharge transistors that are already built into the hardware.
contributions: Novel DRAM cache architecture optimized to operate as Last-Level Cache with high set-associativity
In-subarray tag matching and way selection mechanism for reduced latency
Repurposing precharge transistors for efficient tag matching operations
Caching-In-Memory design achieving significant performance and energy efficiency gains
primary_theme: DRAM-based cache architecture for data centers
